carried_forward.title: A schedule's canonical digest can be overridden via the constructor and does not survive a SQLite round-trip as content identity
carried_forward.recommendation: Mirror Capability::Descriptor: compute the canonical digest after validate!, require equality when a digest is supplied, raise Tamoz::ConfigurationError, and freeze the value.
carried_forward.delta: New: a malformed override ('not-a-digest') is also accepted silently. New positive: the no-override round trip does preserve the canonical digest.

carried_forward.title: Completion accepts an execution id different from the one acknowledged for the running occurrence
carried_forward.recommendation: Store half is F07-owned (compare the recorded execution id in the completion transaction). Add the value-level guard in transition_from_running: refuse when reason['execution_id'] is present and differs, raising the existing SchedulerError.
carried_forward.delta: Broadened: the mismatch is accepted by the gem's own value state machine with no store involved, so part of this finding sits inside F05's surface.

carried_forward.title: Worker settlement requires two SQLite-only occurrence methods absent from the versioned store contract
carried_forward.recommendation: Promote acknowledge_occurrence and occurrence_for_request into the versioned contract with a deliberate revision, or define a separate required worker extension that fails fast before materialization.
carried_forward.delta: Unchanged. Not re-litigated; carried by name.

findings.title: The :latest misfire ledger has no age or count bound, contradicting the finite / no-unbounded-backlog documentation
findings.recommendation: Make misfire_limit bind for the coalescing policies in misfire_selection (cap skipped at misfire_limit, record the remainder as coalesced), and correct documentation/design/scheduling.md:55 to name the policy it applies to. No pruning job, no retention column. Add one store test asserting a bounded ledger after a long outage.
findings.probe: due(now: anchor+1_000_000, limit: 10) on a 3600s cadence -> skipped.size == 9 in one scan; misfire_limit is read only in the :replay branch; no maximum-age column exists in the schema

findings.title: A lost consumer wedges a forbid schedule permanently: no occurrence expiry, reclaim, or recovery path exists
findings.recommendation: Pick one direction, not both. (a) Recommended: delete the lease fiction - drop lease_for from materialize_due, remove the reclaim clause from LeaseLostError, remove or wire ClockRollbackError, and revise SCHEDULER_DESIGN.md:107-124 to the shipped atomic-enqueue model - plus a worker-side guard that emits a typed signal once and refuses further skipped growth for a stuck occurrence. (b) Alternative: honor it by treating a non-terminal occurrence older than the published lease as reclaimable. Add a regression that polls past a lost consumer and asserts a bounded, converging ledger.
findings.probe: poll1 claimed=1, occurrence left :enqueued; polls 2-4 claimed=0 each and appended :skipped; an operator put_schedule edit did not unblock it; respond_to?(:reap/:recover_occurrence/:renew_occurrence_lease/:claim_due) all false; complete_occurrence from :enqueued correctly refused; final ledger [:skipped, :enqueued, :skipped x 7]

findings.title: max_concurrency: 0 makes an :allow schedule permanently and silently undeliverable
findings.recommendation: Reject max_concurrency < 1 in validate_policies!/validate_limit! using the existing Tamoz::ConfigurationError path and the wording already used for budgets. Add one value test asserting max_concurrency: 0 raises.

findings.title: Schedule signals carry an empty correlation list and cannot distinguish backpressure from a dead schedule
findings.recommendation: Add %i[occurrence_id] to the correlation list of tamoz.worker.schedule.materialized (the value is already passed) and emit the stuck-occurrence condition once per schedule instead of only as a low-cardinality reason string.

findings.title: materialize_due does not advance calculation state, though the design says it does
findings.recommendation: Correct the doc sentence only. The simple solution already delivers the property: in-transaction occurrence_exists? plus PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE is the real idempotence mechanism. Recommend no code change.

findings.title: The published ScheduleStore contract names three methods that do not exist, and the scheduling design states DST handling in the present tense
findings.recommendation: Replace the claim_due/renew_occurrence_lease/enqueue_occurrence listing with the shipped surface, and move the DST fold/gap paragraph to the deferred section so the page agrees with limitations.md:79-86. Same seam as F05-REL-05 recommendation (a).

findings.title: current_grant is a caller-supplied keyword with no provenance check at the fail-closed seam
findings.recommendation: None. Verified boundary fact: the in-tree caller supplies @runtime.worker_grant derived from operator policy, so no widening is reachable. Recorded so the guarantee is not mistaken for a property of the seam.

civil_time_boundary.cron: rejected with a typed Tamoz::ConfigurationError; recorded deferral
civil_time_boundary.at_can_express: exactly one absolute UTC instant, canonical YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, validated as a real calendar instant by round-trip; fires at most once ever
civil_time_boundary.interval_can_express: anchor + k*N integer seconds for k >= 0, anchor = start_at || created_at; oldest-first, truncated from the oldest end by the scan limit
civil_time_boundary.cannot_express: any IANA timezone, local time, civil calendar rule, DST gap/fold, weekday selection, date-only trigger, sub-second precision, event stream, filesystem watcher, or arbitrary trigger script
civil_time_boundary.doc_delta: documentation/design/scheduling.md:59 states DST 'nonexistent_local_time' and a fold 'both' option in the present tense; neither string appears in any gem source. documentation/limitations.md:79-86 is the accurate page.
